race_context: Westfield Washington Schools (WWS) serves Westfield and Washington Township in Hamilton County. The district says it serves more than 10,400 students and 8,400 families across 16 facilities with more than 1,600 employees {rep_wws_ref}. Dr. John Atha is superintendent {rep_wws_ref} {wws_atha_ballot}.

The Board of School Trustees has five members. Four are elected from geographic districts and the fifth seat is at-large, covering the whole township {wws_districts}. 2026 officers are Rebecca Ogle (president), Bill Anderson (vice president) and Carrie Larrison (secretary); Amber N. Willis and Mike Steele are members {rep_reorg} {wws_board}.

Three of the five seats are on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot, and each race elects one member. District 2 is held by Bill Anderson (first elected 2018), District 4 by Rebecca Ogle (first elected 2018) and the at-large seat by Amber N. Willis (on the board since January 2015) {wws_anderson} {wws_ogle} {wws_willis}. All three incumbents are on the ballot: Anderson is unopposed in District 2, Ogle faces Steven Castle in District 4, and Willis faces Gabriel Crawford-Paree at large {in_list}. Mike Steele (District 3) and Carrie Larrison, sworn in January 2025, are not up this year {wws_board} {rep_larrison}.

Party labels: 2026 is the first election cycle under Senate Bill 287 (2025), which lets school board candidates list a party on the ballot {rep_sb287}. On the state list, Anderson, Ogle and Willis are listed as Republicans, Crawford-Paree as a Democrat and Castle as nonpartisan {in_list}.

Referendum: on June 9, 2026 the board voted unanimously to put an eight-year operating referendum on the ballot (Public Question 3), with a maximum rate of $0.3941 per $100 of assessed value and a maximum annual levy of $38 million. The district says the money would go to safety (including school resource officers), staffing, transportation, academic programs and student support {rep_wws_ref}. It would replace the current $0.17 referendum, which voters approved in 2022 and which expires at the end of 2026 {wws_ref_page}.

Referendum cost: the state-required ballot language shows an $873 annual increase for a $450,000 home. Chalkbeat reported that, because the new rate replaces the current one, the district puts the increase closer to $494 for that home {cb_ref}. The district estimates a net increase of about $147.68 a year for the actual median home ($426,700) after the SEA 1 homeowner credit, and its tax calculator uses a rate of $0.3381 rather than the $0.3941 maximum {wws_ref_page}. In an Oct. 8 column, Atha called the state-required ballot wording "misleading" because it uses a rounded-up home value and the maximum rate, and does not subtract the existing referendum {wws_atha_ballot}.

Budget and SEA 1: in June, district projections cited a funding gap of about $14.8 million in 2026, linked to below-average state funding, property-tax caps and the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) {rep_wws_ref}. The district's referendum page gives other figures: a $15.1 million gap and a projected gap of about $17.5 million "in the coming years" {wws_ref_page}. The OneZone Chamber board endorsed the referendum {rep_onezone}.

Growth and facilities: the district calls itself the fastest-growing school district in Indiana. For 2026-27, fifth grade moved to the elementary schools and two new elementary schools opened, and a second middle school opens in 2027-28. A rebalancing committee finished new boundaries on Oct. 8, 2025, moving about 34% of elementary students {wws_rebal}. In January 2026 the board hired an architect for a Westfield High School renovation and expansion estimated at $88 million in construction, built in phases through summer 2028 {rep_reorg}. In January the board and the City Council also held a joint work session on growth and enrollment projections {rep_joint}.

Academics and schedule: on March 10, 2026 the board approved moving Westfield schools from trimesters to semesters starting in 2027-28 {rep_semester}. The district reported 2026 ILEARN proficiency of 65.2% in math and 61.2% in English language arts, compared with 42.7% and 42% statewide {rep_ilearn}.

Forums and coverage: no 2026 candidate forum or questionnaire for these races turned up in the sources reviewed. The superintendent scheduled community presentations on the referendum in September and October {rep_wws_meetings}. Anderson and Ogle share a joint campaign website {ws_home}. Crawford-Paree has a campaign website {cp_site}. No campaign website or public statements were found for Willis or Castle.

candidates.summary: Incumbent, unopposed in District 2. Board member since 2018 and current vice president, listed as a Republican {wws_anderson} {rep_reorg} {in_list}.
background: Goes by Bill Anderson on district and campaign materials. Elected to the District 2 seat in November 2018 {wws_anderson}.
IT project manager for a contractor that serves as fiscal agent for the state Family and Social Services Administration's Office of Medicaid Policy and Planning {wws_anderson}.
Graduate of Indiana University Bloomington (public affairs management, minor in economics); grew up in Fort Wayne {wws_anderson}.
Longtime Westfield resident whose son graduated from Westfield High School in 2022. Has volunteered with schools, Westfield youth sports and Kiwanis {wws_anderson} {ws_anderson_about}.
path_to_ballot: Appears on the ballot as a Republican, with no opponent in District 2 {in_list}.

items: His campaign site lists "Serving all of the children in the community and keeping them safe" as a focus {ws_anderson_why}.
His campaign site lists a long-term plan to "retain and attract the best and the brightest" to the district {ws_anderson_why}.
Says a school board "must be responsive and receptive to parents, staff, students and the community at large" {ws_anderson_why}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. A joint campaign site with Ogle says the two ran on a list of commitments in 2018 and 2022 and asks voters to re-elect them {ws_home}. In June 2026 he was part of the unanimous vote to place the operating referendum on the ballot {rep_wws_ref}.
plans: Says he wants to create a long-term vision for the educational opportunities students need {ws_anderson_why}.
gaps: The ballot lists him as William Wayne Anderson. District and campaign materials use Bill Anderson.

The campaign-site text appears to have been written for earlier campaigns (it refers to 'running' and lists 15 years of IT work, while the district bio says 20). No 2026-specific statements on the referendum, budget or SEA 1 were found.
Search snippets of a June 18, 2026 article in Current in Westfield (which could not be fetched) said he has served as board secretary, vice president and president. Unverified.
No endorsements, fundraising reports or forum appearances were found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent, current board president and a certified public accountant. Listed as a Republican, she faces Steven Castle {wws_ogle} {rep_reorg} {in_list}.
background: Elected to the District 4 seat in November 2018; board president in 2026 {wws_ogle} {rep_reorg}.

CPA and certified fraud examiner. Spent 22 years in public accounting, where she became a partner, focusing on construction and forensic accounting. Has been chief financial officer of Kort Builders since August 2023 {wws_ogle}.
Serves on the City of Westfield's Road Impact Fee Review Board and Audit Committee; former treasurer of Westfield Youth Sports, Inc. {wws_ogle}
Moved to Westfield in 2002, she says because of the schools. Her children are Westfield High School graduates {wws_ogle} {ws_ogle_about}.
path_to_ballot: Appears on the ballot as a Republican {in_list}.

items: Her campaign site lists a focus to "Proactively manage spending and be a steward of referendum funds" and says her accounting background makes her suited to "shepherd our schools through referendum spending and related financial issues" {ws_ogle_why}.
Lists protecting "qualified teachers and staff" as a priority {ws_ogle_why}.
Lists "Protect our kids" as a priority {ws_ogle_why}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member and the board's 2026 president {rep_reorg}. The joint campaign site with Anderson asks voters to re-elect them based on commitments made in 2018 and 2022 {ws_home}. In June 2026 she was part of the unanimous vote to place the operating referendum on the ballot {rep_wws_ref}.
plans: Says she will bring accounting and finance practices to board discussions and decisions {ws_ogle_about}.
gaps: The campaign-site text appears partly written for earlier campaigns. No 2026-specific statements on the referendum, SEA 1 or the high school renovation were found.
No endorsements, fundraising reports or forum appearances were found.

candidates.summary: Challenger in District 4, listed as nonpartisan on the state candidate list {in_list}.
path_to_ballot: Appears on the ballot with no party affiliation, against incumbent Rebecca L. Ogle {in_list}.
gaps: No campaign website, social media page, news profile, questionnaire or forum appearance was found. His background and positions are unknown.
A June 18, 2026 article in Current in Westfield (which could not be fetched) reportedly described him as unaffiliated with a political party. Its full text could not be checked.

candidates.summary: Incumbent at-large member since January 2015, seeking a fourth term. Listed as a Republican, she faces Gabriel Crawford-Paree {wws_willis} {in_list}.
background: Has served as the at-large trustee since January 2015 and is in her third term {wws_willis}.
Lifelong Westfield resident and 1999 graduate of Westfield schools; graduated from Miami University in 2003 {wws_willis}.

Works for her family's business, CSI Signs. Has been a member of the Westfield Education Foundation and the Westfield Business Development Committee and is a Hamilton County Leadership Academy alumna {wws_willis}.
Parent of students in the district, according to her district bio {wws_willis}.
path_to_ballot: Appears on the ballot as a Republican {in_list}.

items: Her district bio quotes her goal of "Connecting the Community to the Children" and says students are "the most important stakeholders in everything the School Board decides" {wws_willis}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. In June 2026 she was part of the unanimous vote to place the operating referendum on the ballot {rep_wws_ref}. No 2026 campaign statements about the board's record were found.
gaps: The ballot lists her as Amber Huff Willis. District materials use Amber N. Willis.
No 2026 campaign website, questionnaire or forum appearance was found. Her positions come only from her district board bio, which may date from an earlier term.
Search snippets said she won the at-large seat in 2022 against three challengers with 8,002 votes (Current in Westfield). Unverified.
No endorsements or fundraising reports were found.

candidates.summary: Engineer, Westfield resident and first-time candidate running as a Democrat for the at-large seat, against incumbent Amber Huff Willis {cp_site} {in_list}.
background: Engineer who grew up in Hamilton County and graduated from Fishers High School (Hamilton Southeastern Schools) in 2016; now lives in Westfield {cp_site}.
His campaign site says he wants to build on the schools' quality and plans to send future children to WWS {cp_site}.
path_to_ballot: Appears on the ballot as a Democrat {in_list}. His site says he filed with a party label, allowed under the 2025 law (SB 287). He says he is not running as a Democrat to bring partisanship to the board, but because he believes support for public schools has become a partisan issue, citing voucher programs {cp_site}.

items: Lists supporting and retaining teachers as his top priority, including a review of "any administrative burden interfering with day-to-day operations" {cp_site}.
Wants better transparency and community engagement through "more robust communications and documentation" {cp_site}.
Proposes exploring a parental advisory committee to bring parents into board discussions more regularly {cp_site}.
Wants a "robust system" so all students can succeed, including those with more specialized needs and those who have been bullied {cp_site}.
Proposes adding guidance on artificial intelligence to board policy so teachers have guardrails for teaching about it {cp_site}.

on_incumbent: His site says he would bring "a unique perspective not currently represented on the school board." It contains no specific criticism of the current board's decisions {cp_site}.
plans: Describes his approach as an engineer's problem-solving: gathering information from stakeholders before deciding {cp_site}.
endorsements_finance: His campaign takes online donations through ActBlue and is paid for by the Election Committee of Gabriel Crawford-Paree {cp_site}. No contribution totals were found.
gaps: Search snippets of a June 18, 2026 article in Current in Westfield (which could not be fetched) said he moved to Westfield in 2022 and wants more informative board agendas and easier public comment at meetings. Unverified.
No stated position on the 2026 operating referendum was found.
No forum appearances, questionnaires or endorsements were found.
